sentences.text: Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal I.A. No.9770/2025, an application for change of counsel is dismissed as there is no appellant No.4 in the present appeal, whereas in paragraph 2 of the application it is mentioned that it is on behalf of appellant No.4.

Though Shri Manoj Kushwaha, learned counsel submits that he be permitted to assist Shri Khalid Noor Fakhruddin, but fact of the matter is that when application for change of counsel is filed without application of mind and without bringing correct facts on record, then such application deserves to be and is hereby dismissed.

2. Shri Khalid Noor Fakhruddin, learned counsel for the appellant instead of pressing I.A.
No.14178/2023 which is first application for suspension of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:21390 2 CRA-10114-2022 sentence and grant of bail to appellant Imran S/o Haleem Mohammad, prays that this appeal be heard finally.

3. Accordingly, I.A. No.14178/2023 is dismissed as not pressed and with the consent of the parties,
this appeal is heard finally.

It is submitted by Shri Khalid Noor Fakhruddin, learned counsel for the appellant that Prosecutrix (PW-4) admitted that she had left from her house at Panna to Satna on her own volition where she had met the appellant.

She also admitted that in her 164, Cr.P.C. statements she had stated that she was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21390 3 CRA-10114-2022 in love relationship with the appellant, a fact which was known to her parents and objected by her parents.
It is further submitted that age of the prosecutrix is doubtful.
PW-2 school teacher has been examined who stated that the prosecutrix had taken admission in class 7th and after passing class 7 th and 8 th, she was given TC.
Prosecution has neither produced first school entry register nor any TC has been produced on record on the basis of which date of birth of the prosecutrix was recorded in the school record.
father of the prosecutrix admitted that he does not know age of any of his three children or their date of birth and stated that the prosecutrix was admitted by mother in class-1.
He states that he had no information if any Samagra ID, which was prepared in 2013, makes mention of age of the prosecutrix to be 16 years.

mother of the prosecutrix admitted that she also does not remember date of birth of any of her children and further admitted that the prosecutrix was admitted in a private school near Kishore Ji mandir by her mother-in-law along with her and then she improvised her statements and said that admission of the prosecutrix and other children were made by her mother-in-law.
She stated that she cannot say as to which date of birth of the prosecutrix was recorded by her mother-in-law in the school register.
She further stated that mother-in-law used to go inside the school and this witness used to stay outside the school along with her children.
She admits that she cannot say that whether mother-in-law had taken any document for admission of the prosecutrix or not.

She admits Imran vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156125920/
2 that she got her Samagra ID prepared on 14.03.2013 in which age of the prosecutrix is mentioned as 16 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21390 4 CRA-10114-2022 years.

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the prosecutrix at the time of the incident was major.

She was a consenting party,
therefore, aforesaid conviction is not maintainable.
It is also submitted that the DNA report (Ex.P-21) is uninterpretable and, therefore, no reliance can be placed on the said uninterpretable DNA profile.
Thus, it is submitted that it is a fit case for acquittal of the appellant.
8. Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Public Prosecutor supports the impugned judgement of conviction and submits that no interference is called for in the same.

He further submits that the prosecutrix admitted that she was taken by the appellant to Delhi where her privacy was continuously violated against her will and that is a sufficient circumstance to uphold the conviction recorded by the learned trial Court.
9. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, first aspect is in regard to the age of the prosecutrix.
Mother of the prosecutrix admitted that when she got Samagra ID prepared for the family on 14.03.2013, at that time she had recorded age of the prosecutrix to be 16 years.
Admittedly the incident took place on 22.04.2018.
Therefore, the prosecutrix was about 21 years of age when the incident took place.
10. Both father and mother of the prosecutrix i.e. PW-5 and PW-6 have admitted that they are not aware about the date of birth of the prosecutrix or any of their children.

Thereafter, mother of the prosecutrix (PW-6) admits that admission of the prosecutrix was made by her mother-in-law and she has no intimation as to on what basis, date of birth of the prosecutrix was recorded in the school records. PW-2 school teacher

admitted that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21390 5 CRA-10114-2022 prosecutrix had come to their school to take admission in class 7th along with TC of class 6th, but TC of class 6 th is not exhibited on record.
Thereafter, the prosecutrix had taken TC on 22.06.2018.
He admitted that there is no photograph affixed on the scholar register or on the admission form.
Though he stated that there is no provision for affixing photograph on scholar register, but admits that on admission form, photograph is required to be affixed.
Thus, it is evident that even PW-2 has not been able to bring on record any documentary evidence on the basis of which date of birth of the prosecutrix was recorded in the school records.
11. As far as PW-3 Dr. Harshita Sharma is concerned, she stated that mental status of the prosecutrix was normal.
Her secondary sexual characters were developed.
There were no external or internal injury marks on her body.
Her UPT was negative.
This witness also admitted that there were no internal injury marks on the body of the prosecutrix.
MLC report is Ex.P-6 on which her signatures are from 'A' to 'A' part.

12. When all these facts are taken into consideration so also the fact that the prosecutrix herself admitted that she was knowing the appellant and had travelled from Panna to Satna to be in the company of appellant, from where appellant had taken her to Delhi, it is evident from record that the prosecutrix was major at the time of the incident.

Prosecution has failed to prove that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident, therefore, when tested, then prosecutrix was a consensual party and therefore, conviction under Sections 363, 366, 343, 376(2)(n) of IPC or under Imran vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156125920/
3 Sections 5/6 of POCSO Act, 2012, cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.

sentences.text: Moreover, it has not come on record NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21390 6 CRA-10114-2022 that privacy of the prosecutrix was subjected to any oppression or hardship on account of she being a member of scheduled caste category, therefore, conviction under 3(2)(5) or 3(2)(5-A) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is also not sustainable in the eyes of law.
Accordingly, impugned judgment of conviction is hereby set aside.
13. In the result, appeal filed by the appellant is allowed and disposed of.
Appellant be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
The case property be disposed off in terms of the judgment of the trial Court.
Record of the trial Court be sent back.

Pending application(s), if any,
also stand disposed of.
